name: scarecrow
revision: r2 (2026-11-10): the r1 critic's and continuity's must-fixes and the cheap should-fixes applied, see reviews/r1-response.md
caption: who leaves snow under my window? 😨
logline: On a hill farm above his village, where it never snows, Milo finds a trail of snow every morning from Grandpa's scarecrow to his window, stays up to catch his stalker, and throws the window open on the night guard Grandpa left him.
question: why tf is there snow leading to his window when it never snows?
premise: Sixty-three mornings in a row, a trail of snow runs across the green grass from the scarecrow in Grandpa's wheat to Milo's bedroom window, on a hill farm where it never snows. He shovels it up and it's back every night, ending in a trampled patch where someone seems to stand all night staring at him. He hears groaning every night and doesn't look, finds rotten flesh under his window, and Mom said Grandpa built that scarecrow out of snow the week before he died. Grandpa always said he'd keep an eye on him.
twist: The stalker is a guard. Every night zombies come for the boy (a player) and crowd the wall under his window, groaning up at him. The scarecrow is a snow golem Grandpa built: it walks out of the wheat to the spot where it can see them, leaving its vanilla snow trail, and pelts them with snowballs all night, shoving them off his wall until they burn at sunrise (the rotten flesh). He throws the window open expecting the stalker in his face, finds the scarecrow gone from the wheat, and the camera looks down: the zombies were under his window, and the thing staring at him all night was keeping an eye out for him.

requests.direction: [A bubbly nine-year-old kid, fast, bright and energetic, telling a friend an amazing story; not whispery, breathy or soft]

lines.text: SIXTY-THREE mornings / in a row, / a trail of SNOW / runs from our SCARECROW / to my WINDOW.
lines.direction: spooked and excited at once, one quick breath straight through to the end, a tiny lift on the number, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: It never SNOWS here. / I shovel it UP. / It comes BACK.
lines.direction: amazed on the first part, proud on the shoveling, grumpy on the last two words, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: It ENDS / by my window. / Like someone / STOOD there, / STARING at me.
lines.direction: the fun drains out and the creeped-out kid shows, still loud and quick, lean on the last two words, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: EVERY night, / I hear GROANING. / I don't LOOK.
lines.direction: scared but brave-sounding, the last three words fast and firm, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: There's ROTTEN FLESH / under my window. / A GROSS / little GIFT.
lines.direction: grossed out and giggly at the same time, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: Mom said / GRANDPA built that scarecrow / out of SNOW. / The week / before he DIED.
lines.direction: the bounce goes out of it for a moment, plain and a bit sad, still clear, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: He always SAID / he'd keep an EYE / on me. / Kind of CREEPY now.
lines.say: He always said he'd keep an eye on me. <short pause> Kind of creepy now.
lines.direction: warm on the first part, then a quick spooked joke for the last four words, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: So last night, / I stayed UP / to CATCH it.
lines.direction: determined, a detective on a mission, speeding up, full volume, never hushed or breathy

lines.text: The GROANING came. / I threw the window OPEN.
lines.say: <short pause> The groaning came. I threw the window open.
lines.direction: brave and fast, building to a big burst on the last word, ready for a fight, full volume, never hushed or breathy
a real jolt of fear, short and sharp, still full volume, not whispered

lines.text: It wasn't STARING / at me. / It was keeping / an EYE OUT / for me.
lines.say: <short pause> It wasn't staring at me. It was keeping an eye out for me.
lines.direction: warm and bright, a smile in it, full volume, never soft, whispered or breathy
